name: Shepherd's Pie
blurb: Minced lamb in rich gravy under a fluffy mashed potato crust.
method: Brown the mince, then set aside. Soften the onion and carrot for 10 minutes.
Stir in the puree, Worcestershire and thyme, return the lamb, add the stock and simmer 20 minutes. Stir in the peas.
Boil the potatoes, then mash with butter and milk and season well.
Spoon the mince into a dish, top with mash, rough up with a fork and scatter with cheese if using.
Bake at 200C fan for 25 minutes until golden.

name: Cottage Pie
blurb: The beef version: savoury mince and veg topped with golden mash.
ingredients: 2 tbsp tomato puree, 1 tbsp Worcestershire sauce
method: Brown the mince and set aside. Soften the vegetables for 10 minutes.
Add the puree, Worcestershire and thyme, return the beef, pour in the stock and simmer 25 minutes.
Mash the boiled potatoes with butter and milk, season.
Top the mince with mash, fork the surface and bake at 200C fan for 25-30 minutes.

name: Fish Pie
blurb: Smoked and white fish in a creamy sauce under mash, with peas.
ingredients: 600g fish pie mix (salmon, white fish, smoked haddock)
1 bay leaf, handful of parsley and chives
100g frozen peas, 3 eggs, hard boiled and quartered (optional)
method: Poach the fish in the milk with the bay for 4 minutes, then lift out and flake, keeping the milk.
Make a white sauce with the butter, flour and infused milk; stir in the herbs.
Fold the fish, peas and egg through the sauce and tip into a dish.
Top with seasoned mash and cheese, and bake at 200C fan for 30 minutes until golden.

name: Roast Chicken Dinner
blurb: Whole roast chicken with roast potatoes, veg and proper gravy.
ingredients: 1 lemon, halved, few thyme sprigs, 50g soft butter
Carrots, parsnips and greens to serve
Gravy: 1 tbsp flour, 400ml chicken stock, splash of wine
method: Heat oven to 200C fan. Rub the chicken with butter, season, and put the lemon and thyme in the cavity. Roast 70-80 minutes until juices run clear.
Parboil the potatoes 8 minutes, drain and rough up. Roast in hot fat for 45-55 minutes, turning, until crisp.
Boil the carrots and parsnips; steam the greens.
Rest the chicken 15 minutes. Make gravy in the roasting tin with the flour, wine and stock.
Carve and serve everything together.

name: Toad in the Hole
blurb: Sausages baked in crisp, billowing Yorkshire pudding batter with onion gravy.
ingredients: Onion gravy: 2 onions sliced, 1 tbsp flour, 500ml beef stock, splash of Worcestershire
method: Whisk the flour, eggs and milk into a smooth batter and rest 30 minutes. Season.
Heat oven to 220C fan. Put the fat and sausages in a roasting tin and roast 10 minutes until sizzling.
Pour in the batter and bake 25-30 minutes until risen and deep golden. Do not open the door early.
Meanwhile slowly caramelise the onions, stir in the flour, then the stock and Worcestershire, and simmer to a gravy.
Serve the toad in generous squares with the onion gravy.

name: Bangers & Mash
blurb: Grilled sausages, buttery mash and a deep onion gravy.
method: Fry or grill the sausages slowly until browned all over and cooked through.
Boil the potatoes and mash with butter and milk; season generously.
Cook the onions low and slow in butter for 20 minutes until sweet and golden.
Stir the cornflour into a little stock, add to the onions with the rest of the stock, mustard and Worcestershire, and simmer to a gravy.
Serve the sausages on the mash, drowned in gravy.

name: Beef Stew & Dumplings
blurb: Slow-braised beef in ale gravy topped with fluffy suet dumplings.
ingredients: 2 tbsp plain flour, 2 tbsp tomato puree
500ml brown ale, 500ml beef stock, 2 bay leaves
Dumplings: 150g self-raising flour, 75g shredded suet, pinch of salt, water to bind
method: Toss the beef in seasoned flour and brown well in batches in a casserole.
Soften the vegetables, stir in the puree, then add the ale and let it reduce.
Return the beef, add the stock and bay, cover and cook at 150C fan for 2 hours.
Mix the dumpling ingredients to a soft dough, roll into balls, and sit on top of the stew.
Cover and cook 20 minutes, then uncover for 10 more until the dumplings are risen and golden.

name: Cauliflower Cheese with Bacon
blurb: Cauliflower under a sharp cheese sauce and crisp bacon, baked as a main.
ingredients: 50g butter, 50g plain flour (or cornflour for GF), 600ml milk
method: Blanch the cauliflower for 4 minutes, then drain well.
Fry the bacon until crisp.
Make a white sauce with butter, flour and milk; off the heat stir in most of the cheese and the mustard.
Fold the cauliflower and bacon through the sauce in a dish, top with the rest of the cheese and the crumbs.
Bake at 200C fan for 25 minutes until golden and bubbling.

name: Loaded Jacket Potatoes
blurb: Crisp-skinned baked potatoes with cheese, beans and whatever else.
ingredients: Optional: tuna mayo, coleslaw, spring onions
method: Heat oven to 200C fan. Prick the potatoes, rub with oil and salt, and bake directly on the shelf for 70-80 minutes until crisp outside and fluffy within.
Warm the beans.
Split the potatoes, fluff with butter and season, then pile on beans and cheese.
Return to the oven for 3 minutes to melt, or add cold toppings and serve.

name: Full English for Dinner
blurb: Breakfast when you want it: bacon, sausage, eggs, beans, mushrooms and toast.
method: Start the sausages in a low oven or slow in a pan; they take longest.
Fry the bacon, then the mushrooms and tomatoes in the fat.
Warm the beans.
Fry the eggs to order and toast the bread.
Plate everything together, with brown sauce or ketchup.

name: Welsh Rarebit
blurb: A grown-up cheese on toast: sharp cheddar, ale and mustard sauce grilled until blistered.
ingredients: 20g butter, 20g flour, 4 tbsp brown ale or milk
1 tsp English mustard, 1 tsp Worcestershire sauce
method: Melt the butter, stir in the flour for 1 minute, then whisk in the ale to a thick paste.
Off the heat, stir in the cheese, mustard, Worcestershire and yolk to a spreadable mixture.
Toast the bread on one side under the grill.
Spread the mixture thickly on the untoasted side and grill until bubbling and dark gold.

name: Gammon, Egg & Chips
blurb: Pan-fried gammon steaks with fried eggs and oven chips.
ingredients: Peas or grilled pineapple to serve
method: Heat oven to 220C fan. Toss the chips in oil and salt and roast for 25-30 minutes, turning once.
Snip the fat of the gammon so it does not curl, then fry for 3-4 minutes each side until caramelised.
Fry the eggs in the same pan.
Serve the gammon with the chips, eggs and peas.

name: Liver, Bacon & Onions
blurb: Quick-seared lamb's liver with bacon and a sticky onion gravy.
method: Fry the bacon until crisp, then set aside. Cook the onions in the fat until soft and golden.
Stir in the flour, then the stock and Worcestershire, and simmer to a gravy.
Dust the liver in seasoned flour and sear for 1-2 minutes each side; it should stay pink inside.
Return the bacon, nestle in the liver and serve with mash.

name: Chicken & Leek Pie
blurb: Creamy chicken and leek filling under a puff pastry lid.
ingredients: 30g butter, 30g flour, 400ml chicken stock, 100ml creme fraiche
method: Brown the chicken, then set aside. Soften the leeks in butter for 8 minutes.
Stir in the flour, then the stock, and simmer to a sauce. Add the creme fraiche, mustard, thyme and chicken.
Tip into a pie dish and cool slightly.
Top with pastry, seal the edges, cut a steam hole and brush with egg.
Bake at 200C fan for 25-30 minutes until puffed and golden.

name: Corned Beef Hash
blurb: Crisp fried potato and onion with corned beef and a runny egg on top.
ingredients: Brown sauce or beans to serve
method: Fry the onion in oil until soft, then add the potatoes and press down to crisp.
Turn the potatoes, add the corned beef and Worcestershire, and keep frying until crisp in patches.
Fry the eggs.
Serve the hash topped with a fried egg and brown sauce or beans.

name: Lancashire Hotpot
blurb: Slow-cooked lamb and onions under a lid of sliced potatoes.
ingredients: 800g lamb neck fillet or shoulder, sliced
1 tbsp flour, 1 tsp thyme, 2 bay leaves
method: Toss the lamb in seasoned flour and brown, then layer with the onions and carrots in a casserole.
Add the thyme, bay, stock and Worcestershire.
Overlap the potato slices on top, brush with butter and season.
Cover and cook at 160C fan for 1.5 hours, then uncover and cook 30 minutes more until the top is crisp and golden.

name: Sausage & Root Veg Traybake
blurb: Sausages roasted with potatoes, red onion and carrots in honey and mustard.
ingredients: 2 tbsp oil, 1 tbsp honey, 1 tbsp wholegrain mustard
method: Heat oven to 200C fan. Toss the potatoes and carrots with oil and rosemary in a large tray and roast 15 minutes.
Add the sausages and onions and roast 20 minutes.
Drizzle over the honey and mustard, toss, and roast a final 10 minutes until sticky and golden.

name: Macaroni Cheese
blurb: Proper baked mac and cheese with a crunchy top.
ingredients: 1 tsp English mustard, pinch of nutmeg
method: Cook the macaroni 2 minutes short of the packet time and drain.
Make a white sauce with the butter, flour and milk, then melt in most of the cheese with the mustard and nutmeg.
Fold in the pasta, tip into a dish and top with the crumb mix.
Bake at 200C fan for 20 minutes until golden and bubbling.

name: Kedgeree
blurb: Smoked haddock, curried rice, boiled eggs and parsley - dinner or brunch.
ingredients: 2 tbsp mild curry powder, 1 bay leaf
method: Poach the haddock in simmering water for 4 minutes, then flake, discarding skin and bones.
Fry the onion in butter until soft, add the curry powder and bay for 1 minute.
Stir in the rice, add 550ml water, cover and cook 12 minutes until tender.
Fold through the fish, halved eggs, parsley and a good squeeze of lemon.
